rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is among the earliest revelations and came in Mecca years before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وسورة الضحى من أوائل الوحي، نزلت بمكة قبل الهجرة بسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent pause in revelation was natural, like night settling after the dawn's brightness.
rows.anchor: أن فتور الوحي ظاهرة طبيعية، شأنها شأن سجو الليل بعد إشراق الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran gives neither a cause nor duration for the pause; proposed explanations and counts of twelve to forty days add nothing to its central meaning.
rows.anchor: فلأن الذي يعنيه هو جوهر الموقف لا تفصيلاته الجزئية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ākhirah broadly means what comes later, the end or outcome in this life or the next; here it most likely means Muhammad's hoped-for future.
rows.anchor: وفي آية الضحى، يرجع أن الآخرة هي الغد المرجو، مجيئها مع {لَكَ} خاصة بمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised good confirms that God has not abandoned or hated the Prophet and comforts him after the pause.
rows.anchor: وقد أكد الله بهذا الخير الموعود، نفى التوديع والقلى، ليذهب عن رسوله أثر فتور الوحي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A reported interpretation specifies a thousand pearl palaces whose earth is musk, with another report describing them as white pearls.
rows.anchor: ألف قصر من لؤلؤ، ترابهن المسك، وفيهن ما يصلحهن. عن إبن عباس أيضاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fixing the gift at a thousand or a million palaces, of any jewel or soil, constrains the Quran's promise, whose wording extends until complete satisfaction.
rows.anchor: وما أرى ألف قصر في الجنة، أو ألف ألف، من لؤلؤ أو غير لؤلؤ

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others read the gift as victory over enemies, the conquest of Mecca, mass conversion, and major conquests by the caliphs.
rows.anchor: ذهبوا في تفسير العطاء إلى أنه إشارة إلى ما سوف يعطى الله رسوله من الظفر بأعدائه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the gift as intercession and forgiveness for the Prophet's followers, supported by reports about intercession and his satisfaction when their requests are answered.
rows.anchor: لأن الله أمره بالاستغفار للمذنبين، ويرضيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن يجاب طلبه.

rows.speaker: إبن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim rejects the claim that the Prophet cannot be satisfied while any follower remains in Hell: he accepts God's judgment and intercedes only with divine permission.
rows.anchor: فإنه صلوات الله وسلامه عليه، يرضى بما يرضى به تبارك وتعالى

rows.speaker: إبن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim instead takes the gift broadly to include Quran, guidance, followers, renown, victory, and what Muhammad receives after death.
rows.anchor: فهو يعم ما في الدنيا من القرآن والهدى والصر وكثرة الأتباع

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Muhammad Abduh condemns importing discussions of intercession and the Prophet's family into this tafsir as alien to the Quran's religious spirit.
rows.anchor: ما للمفسرين هنا من كلام في الشفاعة، وفي تكريم آل بيت النبوة، حشروه في التفسير حشراً

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh explains the gift as continuing revelation, guidance for Muhammad and his people, the spread of Islam, and their elevation in both worlds.
rows.anchor: توارد الوحي عليك بما فيه إرشاد لك ولقومك، ومن ظهور دينك وعلو كلمنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specifying the gift does the verse an injustice; the grandeur of the promise is best preserved by leaving satisfaction beyond every limit and description.
rows.anchor: والأليق بجلال الموقف أن يكتفي فيه بالرضى على ما أراد البيان القرآني، فوق كل تحديد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: To solve the grammatical objection to the laam before sawfa, al-Zamakhshari posits an omitted subject: the original construction would say that you will be given.
rows.anchor: من تقدير مبتدأ محذوف، وأن يكون أصل العبارة:

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan likewise calls the laam an introductory emphatic particle and supplies an omitted subject, أنت.
rows.anchor: إن اللام هنا لام إبتداء أكدت مضمون الجملة على إضمار مبتدأ أي:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatical rules should be tested against the Quranic expression as the primary witness, rather than forcing an imagined original wording onto it.
rows.anchor: وكان يكفي أن يأتي التعبير في الكتاب العربي المبين، ليكون هو الشاهد والحجة

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Some commentators ask how emphatic laam can accompany the future-marking sawfa, then answer that the gift is certain even if delayed for a benefit.
rows.anchor: كيف يجتمع التوكيد المستفاد من اللام، مع التسويف الصريح في {سَوْفَ} ؟

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh links sawfa to the fact that completion of the religion took twenty years, citing the verse announcing that Islam was completed.
rows.anchor: إن إكمال الدين لم يتم إلا في عشرين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasis on the future is ordinary Arabic; sawfa reassures Muhammad that God's care would continue through his past and future, his earlier and later life.
rows.anchor: إيناساً للرسول المصطفى بأنه كان سوف يظل موضععناية ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reminders of earlier favors reassure Muhammad that God will not leave him: God sheltered the orphan, guided the bewildered, and enriched the needy.
rows.anchor: فهو تعالى يبث في نفس الرسول الطمأنينة ويثبت قلبه بلفته إلى ما أسبغ الله عليه في أولاه من نعم

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi offers a metaphorical reading of yatim as a peerless pearl, meaning Muhammad was unmatched among Quraysh; God gave him Abu Talib as refuge.
rows.anchor: إنه من قولهم درة يتيمة، والمعنى: ألم يجدك واحداً في قريش عديم النظير

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi also records the lighter reading fa-awā, understood as God showing mercy.
rows.anchor: وقرئ: فأوى - بالتخفيف، أى رحم.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rightly calls the pearl metaphor an invented interpretation and takes orphanhood in its ordinary sense of losing one's father, as do Abu Hayyan and al-Raghib.
rows.anchor: إن تفسير يتيم هنا بالدرة اليتيمة، من بدع التفاسير

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines the Quranic orphan as a child separated from his father before reaching puberty.
rows.anchor: اليتم - في آية الضحى - إنقطاع الصبي من أبيه قبل بلوغه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran pairs orphanhood with poverty in eleven passages.
rows.anchor: ويلحظ فيه اقتران اليتم بالمسكنة في أحد عشر موضعاً:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic contexts associate orphanhood with vulnerability: need, abuse of property, failure to honor, violent rejection, and oppression.
rows.anchor: كما ذكر فيه من آثار اليتم: الجور، وأكل المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Muhammad was orphaned at birth and lost his mother and grandfather too, God sheltered him from the social and psychological harms the Quran associates with orphanhood.
rows.anchor: وقد ولد محمد يتيماً، ثم تضاعف يتمه بموت أمه وجده، لكنه تعالى نجاه من آثار اليتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified verb āwā suggests divine safety, protection, and refuge, preparing the Prophet for guidance and the great message.
rows.anchor: ترشيحاً بهذا الإيواء الإلهي - غير المقيد بمتعلق - إلى ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran uses āwā fourteen times, consistently conveying a haven, protection, or refuge, literally or hopefully.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء الفعل من {آوَى} في القرآن، أربع عشرة مرة، لا يخطئ الحس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dalal originally means losing one's way or being bewildered; guidance contrasts with it, first in spatial senses and then metaphorically and religiously.
rows.anchor: أصل الضلال في الاستعمال اللغوي، من فقدان الطريق: أرض مضلة، يضل فيها. والضلة الحيرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Quran often uses dalal for unbelief and falsehood, it retains the physical sense, shown by its repeated association with the path and by 32:10.
rows.anchor: مع بقاء الملحظ الحسي اللغوي الذي هو ضلال الطريق، بدليل إقتران الضلال بالسبيل، عشرين مرة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi attributes to al-Kalbi, al-Suddi, and Muqatil the view that Muhammad followed his people's religion for forty years.
rows.anchor: ذكره "الرازي" معزواً إلى الكلبي والسدي ومقاتل

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators reject the unbelief interpretation because prophets are held immune from major and minor sins before and after their commission, let alone unbelief.
rows.anchor: وأنكره جمهور المفسرين، وردوه بأن الأنبياء يجب أن يكونوا معصومين، قبل النبوة وبعدها

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi alone lists twenty interpretations of dalal here, including losing the direction of prayer, being unable to emigrate, and losing one's way in worldly trade.
rows.anchor: وذهبوا بعد ذلك في تأويل الضلال، مذاهب شتى بلغت، في تفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The timeline rules out reading dalal as trade or a wish to emigrate: Muhammad had left commerce for retreat before revelation, and migration came years after this early surah.
rows.anchor: كف عن شواغل التجارة قبل المبعث منذ آثر الاعتكاف والخلوة في غار حراء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو حيان
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Abu Hayyan report stories that Muhammad was lost in Mecca as a child, lost from Halima, or lost on the road to Syria.
rows.anchor: ضل في شعاب مكة وهو صغير، فرده الله إلى جده، وقيل ضلاله من حليمة مرضعته

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan recounts a dream resolving the verse as Muhammad's people being astray and guided through him, with an omitted noun like people in ask the town.
rows.anchor: وجدك ضالاً فهدى، أي وجد رهطك ضالاً فهداه بك. على حذف المضاف، أي رهط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic usage itself shows dalal need not mean unbelief; Joseph's brothers use it for their father's intense attachment to Joseph.
rows.anchor: وليس الضلال هنا كفراً، وإنما هو الشغف بيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Quranic uses describe passionate love, Moses acting before knowing, or one witness forgetting and needing a reminder; none means unbelief.
rows.anchor: وليس شيء من هذه الآيات بالذي يحمل الضلال فيه، على معناه الاصطلاحي وهو الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the verse through Quranic usage avoids both equating dalal with unbelief and inventing twenty strained interpretations to protect Muhammad from that charge.
rows.anchor: يعفينا من التزام المصطلح في لفظ الضلال بمعنى الكفر، وهو أيضاً يعفينا من تلك التأويلات العشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is implausible to make God's favor consist of returning a lost child to his family or making Muhammad's trade profitable.
rows.anchor: وغريب عندنا كذلك، أن نتصور أن الله من على رسوله، بأنه رده إلى أهله

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines dalal as leaving the straight way, deliberately or by mistake, slightly or greatly.
rows.anchor: إنه ترك الطريق المستقيمة عمداً كان أو سهواً، قليلاً كان أو كثيراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before revelation Muhammad was perplexed: he rejected his people's ways but did not know the straight path or how to escape them.
rows.anchor: فقد كانت حالته قبل المبعث حالة حيرة: عاف حال قومه وأنكرها، ولكن أين الطريق المستقيم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad remained perplexed until revelation guided him to the true religion and clear path; this is also Muhammad Abduh's conclusion.
rows.anchor: ولبث على حيرته أمداً، حتى جاءته الرسالة فهدته إلى الدين القيم وأبانت له سواء السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account makes Abu Hayyan's dream and hypothetical omitted noun unnecessary.
rows.anchor: ونحن بهذا في غنى عما لجأ إليه أبو حيان في رؤياه، من افتراض مضاف محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀʾil means destitute or in need; its association with dependents highlights the material burden that can produce poverty.
rows.anchor: العيلة في اللغة الفاقة والعوز. يقال: عالني الشيء، إذا أعوزني.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran uses the term only here and at 9:28, and in both cases sets it against enrichment.
rows.anchor: ولم ترد المادة في القرآن إلا مرتين:

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Some explain enrichment through a succession of material supports: Abu Talib, Khadija, Abu Bakr, the Helpers, then spoils of war.
rows.anchor: أغناه في صباه بتربية أبي طالب، ولما اختلت أحواله أغناه بمال خديجة

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh says Muhammad inherited only a camel and a female servant, then gained means through trade and Khadija's wealth.
rows.anchor: وكان الرسول فقيراً لم يترك لم والده من الميراث إلا ناقة وجارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abduh may have shortened the material-support story to avoid a chronology problem: this early Meccan surah predates the Helpers and war booty.
rows.anchor: فالسورة مكية مبكرة بلا خلاف، وهذا الغنى بالأنصار والغنائم قد كان بعد الهجرة

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: To explain the later wealth in an early revelation, commentators say it was already known to God, making the prophecy miraculous.
rows.anchor: إن هذا كله كان من معلوم الله، وهو كالواقع، فيكون من قبيل الإخبار بالغيب

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Others understand enrichment as contentment, inward wealth, patience, or sufficient provision; al-Raghib distinguishes divine independence, richness of soul, possessions, and abstinence.
rows.anchor: احتمال أن يكون الغنى هو القناعة، وغنى القلب، والصبر، والكفاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic usage first shows that enrichment is not synonymous with material riches.
rows.anchor: أن الغنى فيه غير مرادف للثراء الذي لم يستعمله القرآن قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across many Quranic passages, aghnā means to avail, protect, or suffice rather than to make wealthy, so wealth cannot explain the verb in any of those examples.
rows.anchor: ولا يمكن أن يفسر الإغناء في أي موضع منها بالإثراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In other passages ghina also means being self-sufficient or independent, as with those who turn away from faith or seek no aid.
rows.anchor: وجاء الغنى بمعنى الاستغناء، في مثل آيات:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran distinguishes inner sufficiency from money: ascetic poor people may be counted rich, while money cannot save its owners.
rows.anchor: وفرق القرآن بين الغنى والمال، فقد يكون الغنى مع الفقر المالي كما في:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghani is a divine name used seventeen times in the Quran, but al-Tharī is not among God's names.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في القرآن سبع عشرة مرة، وليس من أسمائه تعالى "الثري".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Quran sometimes uses ghina for wealth, Muhammad did not become rich after his mission or materially change his simple, contented life, even after receiving spoils.
rows.anchor: بل لا نعرف أن مستوى حياته قد تغير مادياً، بعد أن أفاء الله عليه ما أفاء من غنائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enriched Muhammad by contentment and meeting his needs, protecting him inwardly from the humiliating effects of poverty, orphanhood, and bewilderment rather than giving him wealth.
rows.anchor: وإنما أغناه الله بالتعفف وسد الحاجة، فلم يذله فقر المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's care did not restore Muhammad's dead father or fill his treasury; it preserved his character and prepared him psychologically for the message.
rows.anchor: وليست وقاية مادية ترد إليه أباه الذي مات قبل مولده، وتملأ خزانته بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the heart-verb wajada foregrounds the Prophet's inner state and emotional reassurance, rather than merely listing external circumstances.
rows.anchor: الفعل {وَجَدَ} وهو من أفعال القلوب ولم يقل مثلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted objects after sheltered, guided, and enriched are not merely for rhyme: the open wording can include both Muhammad and those helped through his mission.
rows.anchor: ونضيف إليها فائدة الإطلاق، فتحتمل: فآواك وآوى برسالتك اليتامى والمستضعفين

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators explain not oppressing an orphan as refusing to seize the orphan's property or rights because of vulnerability.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون هنا في قهر اليتيم: لا تغلبه على ماله وحقه لضعف حاله.

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan broadens oppression to harmful domination and denying the orphan's due.
rows.anchor: إنه التسلط بما يؤذى، ومنع اليتيم حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emotional reach of fa-lā taqhar is deeper than avoiding theft or overt harm: even a careless word, hurtful tone, or sharp gesture can wound an orphan.
rows.anchor: بحيث تتأثر بالكلمة العابرة، واللفتة الجارحة عن غير قصد، والنبرة المؤلمة بلا تنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qahr means domination; in the Quran its forms describe God, with al-Qahhār paired with al-Wāḥid in all six occurrences.
rows.anchor: وكل قاهر، وقهار، وفي القرآن الكريم، من صفات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A created person must not dominate another, especially a vulnerable orphan; Pharaoh's claim to be above them usurps divine authority.
rows.anchor: فكيف باليتيم المحتاج إلى الرعاية والعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere the Quran depicts harsh treatment of orphans as violently pushing them or failing to honor them; the verb qahara itself is reserved here for the orphan.
rows.anchor: وجاء دع اليتيم تكذيباً بالدين في آية الماعون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والنيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and al-Nishaburi offer two readings of the petitioner: a beggar or a seeker of knowledge.
rows.anchor: هو المستجدي، وقيل هو طالب العلم (الزمخشري والنيسابورى)

rows.speaker: إبن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says the command includes both the petitioner for charity and the seeker of knowledge.
rows.anchor: يعني: سائل المعروف والصدقة، وطالب العلم.

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari chooses the broadest reading of the petitioner: anyone who has a need.
rows.anchor: واختار "الطبري" كل ذي حاجة.

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh takes the petitioner as someone asking about what he does not know; the author finds this best suited to context and Quranic usage of the root.
rows.anchor: واختار الشيخ محمد عبده: المستفهم عما لا يعلم، وهو عندنا أولى بالمقام

rows.speaker: جمهرة المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators identify the blessing to be proclaimed as prophethood; some specify the Quran.
rows.anchor: أما النعمة، فهي النبوة عند جمهرة المفسرين، وخصها قوم بالقرآن

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh reads the blessing as material sufficiency, paralleling the preceding statement that God found Muhammad needy and enriched him.
rows.anchor: واتجه بها الشيخ محمد عبده إلى الغنى بعد عيلة في نسق السورة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari refers the blessing back to the earlier sheltering, guidance, and enrichment; other commentators take it as all blessings.
rows.anchor: أما الزمخشري، فرد النعمة إلى ما سبق من إيواء، وهداية، وإغناء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word niʿma can linguistically carry the reported meanings, while the surrounding command to proclaim it gives this verse a more specific contextual direction.
rows.anchor: وإن كنا نلمح لها في آية الضحى دلالة خاصة، يوحى بها السياق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والفخر الرازي والشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: These commentators caution that speaking of God's blessing is appropriate only without vanity or a desire for notoriety.
rows.anchor: أنه إنما يحسن حين لا يكون ذلك عن رياء أو تشبه بأهل السمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This caution is misplaced for the Prophet, whom God chose as the final messenger and praised for his great character.
rows.anchor: ومن أي السبل يمكن أن نتصور احتمال الرياء والتشبه بأهل السمعة، ممن اصطفاه الله تعالى خاتماً للنبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the verb can mean thanking or publicizing a blessing, the context points to the Prophet proclaiming the message entrusted to him; the blessing is prophethood and revelation.
rows.anchor: هو صريح ما تعلق به مما يتصل بمهمة الرسول التي اصطفى لها، وهو أن يبلغ رسالة ربه

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the needy orphan and petitioner are served before God's own right of thanks because God is rich while they are in need; their due is action, God's is speech.
rows.anchor: إن الله أخر حق نفسه وهو الشكر، وقدم حق اليتيم والسائل، لأنه غني وهما محتاجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordering makes social repair the first concern of the message: relieve the vulnerable, then proclaim the reform and guidance the Prophet was sent to deliver.
rows.anchor: إصلاح الجماعة، يأنى في المنزلة الأولى من الإعتبار والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's first-person plural needs no intermediary or grammatical contrivance; Arabic speakers naturally use the plural when speaking of themselves.
rows.anchor: فلسي تحدث الله جل جلاله عن ذاته بصيغة الجمع، بالأمر الذي يوقف عنده أو يتأول له وسيط ثان

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Some call the addressed prepositional phrases unnecessary additions, saying they clarify an initially vague object.
rows.anchor: وقيل في {لِكِ} هنا، إنها زيادة يستقل المعنى بدونها!!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That proposed clarification would require stopping before لك, but readers unanimously connect the phrase; صدرَك already identifies what was opened, as the following objects do.
rows.anchor: ولا نعلم أحداً من القراء قرأها بالوقف، بل الإجماع على قراءتها وصلاً

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nishaburi describes لك as an insertion and lists possible functions such as generality followed by specification, exclusivity, or emphasis.
rows.anchor: الإجمال ثم التفصيل، وإرادة الاختصاص، أو كونه أهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary Arabic construction needs no extra theory: fronted prepositional phrases naturally strengthen emphasis, exclusive address, and connection.
rows.anchor: وإنما للتقرير وتأكيد الاختصاص وتقوية الإيصال

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh says fronting لك, عنك, and لك before their objects adds emphasis and brings the good news quickly.
rows.anchor: لزيادة التقرير والإسراع بالتبشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary Arabic expressions show that these pronouns are purposeful rather than redundant.
rows.anchor: وإنما هي ضرورة بيانية اقتضاها المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks God to open his chest and make his task easy, illustrating the same construction.
rows.anchor: طه 25: {رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers likewise ask God to forgive their sins and cleanse their misdeeds, illustrating the construction.
rows.anchor: آل عمران 193: {فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍʿ means lowering, casting down, or removing, and is often used for something heavy or burdensome, including childbirth.
rows.anchor: الوضع الحطُّ والإلقاء والطرح زالإسقاط، وأكثر ما يستعمل فيما يثقل ويرْهق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In both literal and figurative Quranic uses, waḍʿ evokes relief from a heavy load: war's burdens, weapons, shackles, and the Prophet's burden.
rows.anchor: فشهد هذا التتبع الاستقرائي، على أن الوضع ملحوظ فيه دائماً، التخفف من ثقل مرهق وحمل باهظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wizr first means a mountain and by extension a refuge; wazīr shares the load, and the term then denotes physical weight or moral sin.
rows.anchor: وأصل الوزر: الجبل، وسمى الملجأ وزراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired image of removing the burden and the burden that made the back give way emphasizes how oppressive its weight had been.
rows.anchor: والوضع للوزر في آية الشرح، يؤكد ثقل العبء، كما تؤكده الآية بعدها

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan quotes linguists who describe a load making a camel's back creak under its weight, like a pot making a noise.
rows.anchor: أنقض الحمل ظهر الناقة إذا سمعت له صريراً من شدة الحمل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the sound a creaking or splitting caused by the weight; Abduh gives a similar explanation.
rows.anchor: هو صوت الانتقاض والانفكاك لثقله

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib rejects making inqāḍ itself the sound: it is the underlying giving way that produces the noise.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الانتقاض ليس الصوت، إنما هو الذي يحدث منه الصوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors a sense of crushing weight that loosens or splits the back, preserving the Quran's broader use of naqḍ for undoing things.
rows.anchor: ونؤثر أن يكون الإنقاض من الإثقال الذي يحل الظهر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib reads the burden as the customs of pre-Islamic ignorance from which Muhammad was specially exempted.
rows.anchor: هو ما كنت فيه من إصر الجاهلية، وأعفيت منه بما خصصت به

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan interprets the burden figuratively as protection from sins and purification from defilement.
rows.anchor: كناية عن عصمته من الذنوب وتطهيره من الأدناس

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari interprets the burden as past sins forgiven and the weight of the Prophet's earlier days lifted.
rows.anchor: وغفرنا لك ما سلف من ذنوبك، وحططنا عنك ثقل أيام الجاهلية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the Prophet had sins that weighed on him, which God forgave.
rows.anchor: كانت للنبي ذنوب قد أثقلته فغفرها تعالى له

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the burden as shirk; the author corrects this to the shirk of Muhammad's people.
rows.anchor: والأولى عندنا أن يقال: الشرك الذي كان فيه قومه.

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Other interpretations include pre-prophetic minor sins, ignorance of revealed laws, intense concern to bring stubborn people to Islam, the burdens of the mission, or pre-revelation bewilderment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما أثقل ظهره لما صدر عنه من بعض الصغائر قبل النبوة

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh reads the image as the crushing psychological burden of concern for his people and uncertainty before revelation, heavier than any physical load.
rows.anchor: ما كان يحمله عليه السلام من ثقل الاهتمام بشأن قومه، وضيق المذاهب بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author agrees with Abduh: the burden is the pre-revelation confusion and failure to find the straight path described in 93:7.
rows.anchor: فالوزر في الآية هو من: ضلال الحيرة وعدم الاهتداء إلى سواء السبيل

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says remembrance can occur in the heart or on the tongue, through recalling something forgotten or maintaining it in memory.
rows.anchor: الذكر ذكران: ذكر بالقلب، وذكر باللسان.

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari explains the raised remembrance as God's name being recalled whenever Muhammad is recalled; Qatada says this holds in both worlds and in prayer and testimony.
rows.anchor: فليس خطيب ولا متشهد ولا صاحب صلاة إلا ينادى بها: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari specifies the Prophet's name paired with God's in the testimony, call to prayer, iqama, tashahhud, sermons, Quranic phrasing, and earlier scriptures' covenant.
rows.anchor: قرن ذكر الرسول بذكر الله في كلمة الشهادة، والأذان، والإقامة، والتشهد، والخطب

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh emphasizes that Muhammad rescued many nations from superstition and corrupt ideas and restored them to sound human nature.
rows.anchor: أن الله هداه إلى إنقاذ أمم كثيرة من رق الأوهام وفساد الأحلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These explanations are complementary and can be gathered under the transmitted interpretation that God raised the Prophet's remembrance.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن ترد جميعاً إلى ما رواه "الطبري" من أقوال أهل التأويل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that dhikr is often attached to God's name or pronoun, while the definite form al-dhikr denotes revelation or the Quran.
rows.anchor: وجاء الذكر معرفاً بأل، بمعنى الوحي أو القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faragha means to become free for something; the future marker and both fa particles signal sequence as well as connection to what precedes.
rows.anchor: فالفراغ متصل السبب بما سبقه من شرح الصدر ووضع الوزر ورفع الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasab can mean exertion and fatigue or standing upright; both meanings are established in Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: والنصب ملحوظ فيه معنى الجهد والتعب، والقيام أو الشخوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic examples distinguish upright setting, as of mountains, from exertion and fatigue, such as travel hardship or labor.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التعب والجهد متعين في آيات:

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib appears to read fanṣab as assigning a specific allotted share, linking nasab to a fixed portion.
rows.anchor: بأن النصب فيها من النصيب، أي القسم المنصوب الشاخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author chooses exertion and effort for fanṣab, supported by all Quranic uses of nasab; al-Nishaburi and Abduh agree, while al-Zamakhshari says diligence and persistence.
rows.anchor: ونؤثر أن نلتفت إلى ما فيه كذلك من معنى الجهد والتعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse deliberately leaves the activity unspecified, consistent with the Quran's practice of leaving open what context already indicates.
rows.anchor: والآية لم تحدد مم يكون هذا الفراغ وفيم يكون النصب

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Reported specifications include turning to prayer after finishing prayer, worship after jihad, or prayer after worldly work.
rows.anchor: إذا فرغت من صلاتك فانصب إلى ربك في الدعاء

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers a general instruction to turn all free time, whether from prayer, jihad, or worldly work, toward worship.
rows.anchor: قول من قال إن الله تعالى أمر نبيه أن يجعل فراغه من كل ما كان مشتغلاً به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari, followed by Abduh, says that after finishing one act of worship Muhammad should follow it with another.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرغت من عبادة فأتبعها أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa links this command to the preceding assurance that relief follows hardship and that God fulfills His promise.
rows.anchor: بسياق الآيات قبلها، بحكم وجود "الفاء" الرابطة للآية بما قبلها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If finishing must be specified, it is the release from confusion, distress, and constriction; once relieved, Muhammad should devote himself to the burdens and struggle of his message.
rows.anchor: هو فراغ اليسر بعد العسر، والراحة النفسية بعد الشدة والكرب، فلينصب المصطفى لتكاليف رسالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Quranic usage outside religious contexts, raghaba denotes strong inclination.
rows.anchor: وجاءت في غير السياق الديني، بمعنى الميل القوي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this construction, fronting ila rabbika makes the desire exclusive to God.
rows.anchor: وهو أسلوب بلاغي يفيد القصر والتخصيص

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says Muhammad should direct his hopes for every need to God alone, unlike his idolatrous opponents.
rows.anchor: أجعل رغبتك إلى ربك دون من سواه من خلقه

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nishaburi says Muhammad should hope in his Lord, not another, for what he longs for and the good of both worlds.
rows.anchor: وأرغب إلى ربك في إنجاز المأمول لا إلى غيره

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh says one should seek recompense for one's deeds from God alone.
rows.anchor: لا ترغب إلى أحد في استثمار أعمالك إلا إلى الله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction ties the exclusive desire for God to the preceding relief and promises, completing the surah's unified movement from distress to ease.
rows.anchor: ووصل الآية بما قبلها، هو الذي يطرد به النسق وتتم وحدة السياق في السورة كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is commonly classified as an early Medinan revelation and sixth in descent order; Mujahid, Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Ata report a Meccan classification.
rows.anchor: وهي مدنية مبكرة، سادسة السور المدنية على المشهور في ترتيب النزول

rows.speaker: مجاهـد وابن عباس والضحاك وعطاء
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Ata are also cited for the opinion that the surah is Meccan.
rows.anchor: وثمة قول بأنها مكية، عن مجاهد وإبن عباس، وعن الضحاك وعطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual distinction is that Meccan revelation establishes doctrine and Medinan revelation treats law, but this Medinan surah shows doctrinal teaching continued.
rows.anchor: ولا يعني هذا أن تخلو السور المكية من أحكام تشريع، ولا أن تخلو المدنية من أصول عامة للعقيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares its afterlife theme with many Meccan surahs, including al-Dhariyat, al-Takwir, al-Infitar, al-Inshiqaq, al-Ghashiya, and al-Qaria.
rows.anchor: الذاريات، التكوير، الإنفطار، الإنشقاق، الغاشية، القارعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Short verses create forceful certainty and convey the decisive danger of the scene without leisurely elaboration.
rows.anchor: أن آياتها قصار، وهذا القصر ملحوظ فيه القوة والجزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite its brevity, the surah repeats elements in eight places; repetition within concise passages reinforces, persuades, and signals decisive judgment.
rows.anchor: نجد التكرار في ثمانية مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's imagery for the Last Day is forceful through violent events and fine details, from earthquakes and blasts to tiny particles and scattered dust.
rows.anchor: والألفاظ المختارة لموقف القيامة، بالغة الإثارة قوية الوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recurrent style shifts the event away from its agent, using passive or intransitive constructions to present the cosmic event itself.
rows.anchor: يصرف الحدث عمداً عن محدثه، فلا يسنده إليه، وإنما يأتي به مبنياً للمجهول
